description: Read every node constraint in the scene. A constraint makes one node (the child) follow another (the parent) every frame — position, rotation and/or scale, with an offset, per-axis selection, mirroring, a look-at mode, a change factor and damping. Unlike studio_attach_object it does not reparent anything, it can link two nodes of two different characters, and it can drive one channel without the others. This is the read-back for the three other studio_constraint_* tools. NodesConstraints is an optional third-party plugin (joan6694): when it is absent this call still succeeds and answers 'available': false with the reason, so check that (or 'plugins.nodes_constraints' in studio_get_info) first. Constraints saved in a scene file come back about eight frames after studio_load_scene returns, so re-read if the list looks empty right after a load.

object_id.description: only return the constraints with this scene object at either end (id from studio_list_objects); 'count' still covers the whole scene

available.description: false when the NodesConstraints plugin is absent or has not initialised; the three write tools then fail with -32001

unavailable.description: why the bridge is unavailable, null when it works

count.description: constraints in the scene, before any object_id filter

id.description: pass this to studio_constraint_set and studio_constraint_delete

enabled.description: false leaves the constraint configured but idle, and restores the child to what it was when the constraint was created

alias.description: the name shown in the NodesConstraints window, empty by default

object_id.description: the scene object this node belongs to

target.description: the node's transform name, or 'root' for the object itself; this is what studio_constraint_create takes

path.description: the same node as a slash path under the object's root — the unambiguous form, also accepted as 'target'

child.description: the node being driven, same shape as 'parent'

position.description: whether the constraint drives the child's position

look_at.description: rotation mode: instead of copying the parent's rotation, the child is turned to face the parent's position

mirror_position.description: the child moves opposite to the parent instead of with it

position_offset.description: [x, y, z] in the parent's local space; [0,0,0] puts the child exactly on the parent

rotation_offset.description: [x, y, z] euler degrees, applied after the parent's rotation

scale_offset.description: [x, y, z] multipliers against the parent's world scale; [1,1,1] copies it

position_factor.description: how much of the parent's movement since the constraint was created reaches the child; 1 = the offset is held exactly, 0 = the child stays put, 2 = it moves twice as far

position_damp.description: 0 = the child snaps every frame; above 0 it lags behind, higher being tighter

position_locks.description: [x, y, z] booleans: true means the constraint drives that axis, false means the child keeps its own value there

reset_position.description: whether disabling or deleting the constraint puts the child's position back where it was when the constraint was created

fix_dynamic_bone.description: skip this constraint in the per-frame pass so a dynamic bone (hair, skirt, breast) keeps driving the child; only has an effect while the Timeline plugin is installed
